Quip

KWIP · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Quip is a witty remark or joke.

"I'm not lazy," she shot back with a quick quip, "I'm just running on a different clock than the rest of you."

Worked Example

His favorite quip about Mondays got a groan and a laugh from the whole office every single week.

The line was short, familiar, and delivered for a quick laugh -- exactly the shape of a quip, as opposed to a longer story or joke.

How Quip Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

wisecrack

wisecrack: a clever, often sarcastic remark

one-liner

one-liner: a short joke delivered in a single line

Antonyms

lament

lament: a serious expression of sorrow or regret

How Strong Is It? — comment → quip → roast

comment vs. quip

comment vs. quip: A comment is a plain, neutral remark; a quip adds wit and a punch of humor to it.

roast vs. quip

roast vs. quip: A roast goes much further than a single quip, stringing together many sharp jokes aimed pointedly at one person.

Build the Word

The pieces

Put it together

Put it together: Quip likely comes from Latin quippe, 'indeed, of course' -- a word once used to introduce a sharp, pointed retort, which slid into English as the name for the retort itself.

Use the root in a new word: quibble

Use the root in a new word: quibble: Quibble is unrelated in meaning but was once thought to share this same origin -- both name a kind of small, sharp verbal jab, whether a witty remark or a petty objection.

Strength Check

Word Choice

Quip always implies brevity and quick wit -- if a remark takes more than a sentence or two to land, it's stopped being a quip.
